simple: the "stuff" of electricity: tiny particles carry it, and it can be positive or negative.
analogy: the water itself in the restaurant's pipes.
precise: electric charge is a property of particles such as electrons (negative) and protons (positive); it is measured in coulombs (C).
source: D2 of F1-01 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D3 of F1-01 (BIPM, "The International System of Units (SI)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much charge flows past a point each second.
analogy: how much water flows through a pipe each second.
precise: the rate of flow of charge, I = Q ÷ t for a steady flow; measured in amperes (A); one ampere is one coulomb per second.
source: D2 of F1-01 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D3 of F1-01 (BIPM, "The International System of Units (SI)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the push that makes charge move, measured between two points.
analogy: the difference in water pressure between two places in the plumbing.
precise: the potential difference between two points: the energy given to (or taken from) each coulomb of charge that moves between them; measured in volts (V), where one volt is one joule per coulomb.
source: D2 of F1-01 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D3 of F1-01 (BIPM, "The International System of Units (SI)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the "height" of one point, compared with a chosen zero point.
analogy: how high a tap is above the basement floor.
precise: the voltage of a point measured from a chosen reference point; only differences of potential have physical meaning.
source: D2 of F1-01 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the point we agree to call 0 V.
analogy: the basement floor from which every height in the building is measured.
precise: the node of a circuit chosen as the 0 V reference for all other potentials; in battery circuits it is usually the battery's − terminal by the designer's choice.
source: D2 of F1-01 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the direction engineers draw current: from + to − outside the battery.
analogy: drawing the water's direction on the building plan.
precise: the direction positive charge would move; in metal wires the electrons actually move the opposite way, and circuit diagrams use the conventional direction.
source: D2 of F1-01 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a tool that shows the voltage between its two probes.
analogy: the plumber's pressure gauge with two hoses.
precise: an instrument (often one mode of a multimeter, F1-07) that displays the potential of its red probe minus the potential of its black probe.
source: D1 of F1-01 (Platt, "Make: Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how strongly a part holds back the current.
analogy: how narrow a pipe in the restaurant's plumbing is.
precise: the ratio of the voltage across a part to the current through it, R = V ÷ I; measured in ohms (Ω).
source: D2 of F1-02 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D3 of F1-02 (BIPM, "The International System of Units (SI)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the unit of resistance.
analogy: a "narrowness number" for a pipe.
precise: one ohm is the resistance through which one volt drives one ampere (1 Ω = 1 V/A).
source: D3 of F1-02 (BIPM, "The International System of Units (SI)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: for many parts, the current is proportional to the voltage.
analogy: twice the pressure through the same pipe gives twice the flow.
precise: V = I × R with R constant; parts that obey it over their working range are called ohmic.
source: D2 of F1-02 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a part made to have a known resistance.
analogy: a pipe section deliberately made narrow.
precise: a two-terminal component manufactured with a stated nominal resistance, a tolerance and a power rating (values from its datasheet).
source: D1 of F1-02 (Platt, "Make: Electronics"); D4 of F1-02 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how far a real part may be from the number written on it.
analogy: pipes from the same shop are never exactly the same width.
precise: the maximum allowed difference between the actual and nominal value, usually given as a percentage in the datasheet.
source: D2 of F1-02 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D4 of F1-02 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a drawing of voltage against current for a part.
analogy: Aiko's table of pressure and cups per minute, drawn as dots.
precise: a plot of the voltage across a part against the current through it; for an ohmic part the points lie on a straight line through the origin whose slope is R.
source: D2 of F1-02 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the ability to do work, such as making light, movement or heat.
analogy: the total effort Kwame spends at the mill during a shift.
precise: a quantity measured in joules (J); in a circuit, each coulomb moved through a voltage V transfers V joules.
source: D2 of F1-03 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D3 of F1-03 (BIPM, "The International System of Units (SI)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how fast energy is delivered or used.
analogy: how hard and how fast Kwame turns the mill at this moment.
precise: the rate of energy transfer, P = E ÷ t; in a part with voltage V across it and current I through it, P = V × I; measured in watts (W), one watt being one joule per second.
source: D2 of F1-03 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D3 of F1-03 (BIPM, "The International System of Units (SI)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: electrical energy turning into heat inside a part.
analogy: the mill's iron body getting warm.
precise: the conversion of electrical power into heat in a resistive part; for a resistor all of P = I² × R is dissipated.
source: D2 of F1-03 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the most power a part may take without damage, as its maker says.
analogy: the mill's sign "do not turn faster than this".
precise: the maximum continuous power dissipation stated in a part's datasheet, under the conditions the datasheet states.
source: D4 of F1-03 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a path with almost no resistance straight across a source.
analogy: a burst pipe that lets the tank empty at once.
precise: an unintended low-resistance connection between two points at different potentials, which lets a large current flow; the current is limited only by the source's internal resistance and the wiring.
source: D1 of F1-03 (Platt, "Make: Electronics"); D2 of F1-03 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: parts connected one after another, so the same current passes through all of them.
analogy: Mr Okafor's way one: one pipe through the sink tap and then the dishwasher valve.
precise: components connected end to end with no branch between them, so they carry the same current; their voltages add.
source: D2 of F1-04 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: parts connected side by side between the same two points, so they share the same voltage.
analogy: way two: the pipe splits, feeds both, and joins again.
precise: components connected between the same two nodes, so they have the same voltage; their currents add.
source: D2 of F1-04 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a meeting point of wires.
analogy: a pipe joint where several pipes meet.
precise: a point (or a set of points joined by wire) in a circuit, which has one potential.
source: D2 of F1-04 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one resistor that would do the same job as a group.
analogy: one pipe that lets through the same flow as a whole set of pipes.
precise: the single resistance that draws the same current from a source as the network it replaces; series: R1 + R2; parallel: 1 ÷ (1/R1 + 1/R2).
source: D2 of F1-04 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two bookkeeping rules: voltages round a loop add to zero; currents into a joint equal currents out.
analogy: water going round the building ends where it started; water into a pipe joint equals water out.
precise: the voltage law: the sum of potential differences around any closed loop is zero; the current law: the sum of currents into any node equals the sum out.
source: D2 of F1-04 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two resistors in series that give a smaller voltage from their middle point.
analogy: a tap halfway down a pipe gives part of the full pressure.
precise: a series pair R1, R2 across Vin whose junction has Vout = Vin × R2 ÷ (R1 + R2) when nothing draws current from the junction.
source: D2 of F1-04 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: when connecting something to a circuit changes the circuit's voltages.
analogy: opening an extra tap halfway down a pipe lowers the pressure there.
precise: the change in a circuit's behaviour caused by the current drawn by a connected load; a load across R2 of a divider forms R2 ∥ Rload and lowers Vout.
source: D2 of F1-04 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a part that stores charge on two plates that do not touch.
analogy: the basement tank with a stretchy rubber wall. [proposed mapping, awaiting registration in guide 8.1; see HW101 NOTES.md]
precise: a two-terminal component made of two conductors separated by an insulator; when a voltage V is applied, charges +Q and −Q collect on the two sides, with Q = C × V.
source: D2 of F1-05 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much charge a capacitor holds for each volt.
analogy: how big and how stretchy the tank's rubber wall is. [proposed mapping, awaiting registration in guide 8.1; see HW101 NOTES.md]
precise: C = Q ÷ V, measured in farads (F); one farad is one coulomb per volt; practical values use µF (10−6 F), nF (10−9 F) and pF (10−12 F).
source: D2 of F1-05 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D3 of F1-05 (BIPM, "The International System of Units (SI)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a resistor and a capacitor together, used to make a delay.
analogy: the rubber-wall tank filled through a narrow pipe. [proposed mapping, awaiting registration in guide 8.1; see HW101 NOTES.md]
precise: a circuit in which a capacitor charges or discharges through a resistance, so its voltage changes gradually rather than at once.
source: D2 of F1-05 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the "speed setting" of an RC circuit: bigger means slower.
analogy: how long the tank takes to fill most of the way. [proposed mapping, awaiting registration in guide 8.1; see HW101 NOTES.md]
precise: τ = R × C, in seconds when R is in ohms and C in farads; after one τ a charging capacitor has covered 1 − e−1 ≈ 63.2 % of the way to the supply voltage.
source: D2 of F1-05 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); R1 of F1-05 (lab run in this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a curve that changes fast at first and then slower and slower.
analogy: the tank fills quickly at first, then creeps towards full.
precise: here V(t) = Vs × (1 − e−t/τ), where e ≈ 2.718 is the base of natural logarithms; in each further τ the remaining gap shrinks by the same factor e−1 ≈ 0.368.
source: D2 of F1-05 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a capacitor with a + leg and a − leg that must not be swapped.
analogy: a tank whose rubber wall may only be pushed from one side.
precise: a capacitor type (for example an electrolytic) that is designed to be used with one terminal always positive; its datasheet gives the polarity marking and the maximum voltage.
source: D1 of F1-05 (Platt, "Make: Electronics"); D4 of F1-05 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a part that lets current through one way and blocks it the other way.
analogy: the one-way flap valve in the restaurant's drain. [proposed mapping, awaiting registration in guide 8.1; see HW101 NOTES.md]
precise: a two-terminal semiconductor device that conducts readily when its anode is more positive than its cathode (forward bias) and passes only a tiny current in the opposite direction (reverse bias), up to its breakdown voltage.
source: D2 of F1-06 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the diode's two ends: current goes in at the anode and out at the cathode.
analogy: the inlet and outlet side of the flap.
precise: in the forward direction, conventional current enters the anode and leaves the cathode; the symbol's triangle points from anode to cathode, towards the bar.
source: D2 of F1-06 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the voltage across a diode when it conducts.
analogy: the pressure needed to hold the flap open.
precise: the voltage across a forward-biased diode at a stated current; it changes only a little over a wide range of current, and its value for a given part comes from the datasheet.
source: D2 of F1-06 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D4 of F1-06 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a diode that gives off light when current flows forward.
analogy: a flap valve that glows while water flows through it.
precise: a light-emitting diode; its colour and forward voltage depend on its semiconductor material, and its brightness rises with forward current up to the datasheet's maximum.
source: D1 of F1-06 (Platt, "Make: Electronics"); D2 of F1-06 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a graph of how much current flows at each voltage.
analogy: a chart of flow against pressure for the stiff flap.
precise: the plot of current against voltage for a part; a resistor's is a straight line (F1-02), a diode's is nearly flat and then rises very steeply.
source: D2 of F1-06 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: what happens if you push a diode backwards too hard: it suddenly conducts and can be destroyed.
analogy: the flap torn off by too much back-pressure.
precise: the reverse voltage above which reverse current rises sharply; the datasheet gives the maximum reverse voltage, which for LEDs can be low.
source: D2 of F1-06 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D4 of F1-06 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one meter that can measure voltage, current and resistance.
analogy: the plumber's pressure gauge, flow meter and pipe tester in one box. [proposed mapping, awaiting registration in guide 8.1; see HW101 NOTES.md]
precise: a test instrument with selectable modes and ranges (at least voltage, current and resistance), connected through two probes to sockets chosen for the mode; the exact sockets, ranges and limits are given in its user manual.
source: D1 of F1-07 (Platt, "Make: Electronics"); D4 of F1-07 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the voltage mode: probes touch the two ends of a part.
analogy: the pressure gauge's two hoses on two joints.
precise: a voltage measurement is made with the meter connected in parallel with the part; an ideal voltmeter draws no current; a real one has a large but finite input resistance.
source: D2 of F1-07 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the current mode: you open the loop and let the current pass through the meter.
analogy: the flow meter fitted into the cut pipe.
precise: a current measurement is made with the meter in series, so the circuit's current flows through the meter's small internal (shunt) resistance; an ideal ammeter has zero resistance.
source: D2 of F1-07 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the resistance mode: the meter sends its own small current through a part.
analogy: testing how narrow a pipe is after taking it out of the building.
precise: a resistance measurement in which the meter applies a known small current or voltage from its own battery; it is valid only with the circuit unpowered, and the part should be isolated from parallel paths.
source: D1 of F1-07 (Platt, "Make: Electronics"); D2 of F1-07 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much the voltmeter itself resists current; bigger is better.
analogy: how little water the gauge's hoses let through.
precise: the resistance a voltmeter presents between its probes; it appears in parallel with the measured part and causes loading (F1-04); its value is given in the meter's manual.
source: D2 of F1-07 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D4 of F1-07 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the small resistance inside the meter in current mode.
analogy: the slight narrowing the flow meter adds to the pipe.
precise: the series resistance an ammeter adds to the circuit; the voltage across it (the burden voltage) slightly reduces the current being measured.
source: D2 of F1-07 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a weak link that breaks on purpose when the current is too high.
analogy: a pipe section designed to burst first, safely, before anything else does.
precise: a protective device that opens the circuit when its current exceeds its rating for long enough; meters usually protect their current inputs with fuses whose ratings are in the manual.
source: D1 of F1-07 (Platt, "Make: Electronics"); D4 of F1-07 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a voltage that changes over time to carry information.
analogy: any message reaching Aiko: the needle's position or the bell's ringing.
precise: a quantity, here a voltage, whose variation in time represents information.
source: D2 of F1-08 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a signal that can take any value in a range.
analogy: the oven thermometer's needle. [proposed mapping, awaiting registration in guide 8.1; see HW101 NOTES.md]
precise: a signal whose value varies continuously and whose exact value carries the information.
source: D2 of F1-08 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D3 of F1-08 (Petzold, "Code") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a signal that is read as one of a few values, usually just HIGH or LOW.
analogy: the order bell: ringing or not. [proposed mapping, awaiting registration in guide 8.1; see HW101 NOTES.md]
precise: a signal interpreted as one of a finite set of levels, in binary logic two (1 and 0), each corresponding to a range of voltages.
source: D2 of F1-08 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D3 of F1-08 (Petzold, "Code") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the line between "counts as LOW" and "counts as HIGH".
analogy: how hard the rope must be pulled before the bell rings.
precise: the input voltage at which a digital input's interpretation changes; real logic families specify ranges guaranteed to be read as LOW or HIGH in their datasheets.
source: D2 of F1-08 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics"); D4 of F1-08 (datasheets/manual of the kit chosen by the owner) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: unwanted wiggles added to a signal.
analogy: Kemal's trembling hand on the bell rope.
precise: unwanted random or interfering variations superimposed on a signal.
source: D2 of F1-08 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: using two thresholds: a higher one to switch on, a lower one to switch off.
analogy: the bell only rings after a firm pull, and only resets after the rope is fully let go.
precise: a property of a circuit whose switching threshold depends on its present state; a Schmitt trigger has an upper threshold for rising inputs and a lower one for falling inputs.
source: D2 of F1-08 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: reading an analog voltage at moments in time and rounding it to one of a fixed set of steps.
analogy: Aiko writing down the thermometer every few minutes, to the nearest mark.
precise: sampling takes values at discrete times; quantisation maps each value to one of 2n codes for an n-bit converter (an analog-to-digital converter, ADC).
source: D2 of F1-08 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a circuit that keeps switching back and forth on its own.
analogy: a kitchen timer that rings, resets itself and rings again.
precise: a circuit that produces a periodic output without a periodic input; a relaxation oscillator does it by charging and discharging a capacitor between two thresholds.
source: D2 of F1-08 (Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
